sentences.text:
1 "(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding the opp.
parties concerned not to take possession over the petitioner's share of land gata no.
174ka area 66.91 square meter (720 square fit), situated in village Ekgharva (Mohammadpur), Pargana Baharaich, Tehsil Ikauna, District- Sharawasti, which is purchased on commercial rates, until full and final payment of compensation on commercial rate to him in the interest of justice.
(ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding the opp.
party no.3 to decide the application dated 16.02.2024 (Annexure No.6) of the petitioner and accordingly pay the compensation on commercial rate, as early as possible in the interest of justice."
3. It has been submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners land were acquired for widening of the National Highway.

They had bought such land of Gata No. 174 (Ka) of Village Ekgharva (Mohammadpur), Pargana- Baharaich, Tehsil - Ikauna, District - Sharawasti for non-agricultural purposes and they have built houses over it and also carried out commercial activities by constructing shops.
The respondents have declared an award and determined compensation treating the land to be agricultural in nature.

The petitioners have already given an application through registered post to the opposite parties no. 4 and 5 stating that Gata No. 174 (Kha) admeasuring 66.91 square meter is a commercial land, and therefore, compensation should be paid to him on the basis of commercial rates as fixed for others similarly situated properties.
They has also made a complaint on the I.G.R.S. Portal.
No heed has been paid till date and the respondents are taken possession over their land.

4. In response to the Court's specific query whether the award passed by the Competent Authority has been challenged by the petitioner under Section 3A(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956, the petitioners have denied making any such challenge.

5. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the Case of Union of India Vs. Kushala Shetty & Other reported in (2011) 12 SCC 69 in para 28 has observed as under :-
"28.

sentences.text: Here, it will be apposite to mention that NHAI is a professionally managed statutory body having expertise in the field of development and maintenance of national highways.

The projects involving construction of new highways and widening and development of the existing highways, which are vital for the development of infrastructure in the country, are entrusted to experts in the field of highways.
It comprises of persons having vast knowledge and expertise in the field of highway development and maintenance.
NHAI prepares and implements projects relating to development and maintenance of national highways after thorough study by experts in different fields.
Detailed project reports are prepared keeping in view the relative factors including intensity of heavy vehicular traffic and larger public interest.
The courts are not at all equipped to decide upon the viability and feasibility of the particular project and whether the particular alignment would subserve the larger public interest.
In such matters, the scope of judicial review is very limited.

sentences.text: In the case in hand, neither has any violation of mandate of the 1956 Act been established nor has the charge of malice in fact been proved.

Therefore, the order under challenge cannot be sustained."
6.
The writ petition, in the manner in which it has been drafted, is not maintainable and it is dismissed as such.
